metadata.title: Three-dimensional relativistic shock hydrodynamics and multi-cluster decoupling without non-baryonic dark matter
metadata.description: The observed spatial decoupling between collisional, X-ray-emitting intracluster plasma and reconstructed gravitational lensing potential centroids in merging galaxy clusters—most prominently in the Bullet Cluster (1E 0657-56)—is widely considered unambiguous empirical proof of non-baryonic collisionless dark matter. We present first-principles 3D relativistic adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) hydrodynamic simulations and Lagrangian kinetic relaxation calculations demonstrating that this spatial separation is a natural consequence of dynamic metric latency in Chronodynamic Relativity. In this framework, the effective gravitational potential Phi(x,t) is a dynamic environmental metric field governed by the non-linear algebraic root law g_eff = 0.5 * [g_N + sqrt(g_N^2 + 4 * g_N * a_c)] with a finite screened relaxation timescale tau_eff approx 80-90 Myr. Across three major cluster mergers, our model reproduces: (1) the Bullet Cluster lensing-gas offset delta r = 331.4 kpc (empirical: 250-350 kpc) and post-shock temperature T_post = 15.22 keV; (2) the El Gordo twin offsets; and (3) the enigmatic Abell 520 dark core via shock stagnation without non-baryonic dark matter particles.
